executive_summary: lib/eva/stage-templates/analysis-steps/stage-15-user-journey.js (live on main since SD-LEO-INFRA-FIRST-CLASS-USER-001, 2026-07-09) has three defects confirmed from both code and live artifact data (AltifyAI venture 50763b6a): story_refs is a synthesized composite pipe-string, never a pointer to a real story, because the story-pack producer never emits a story identifier (18/18 stories, 0 with id/title/name); route is null on 14/14 live steps because it derives from screen.page_type, which is only ever set when the unset, undocumented EVA_SURFACE_AWARE_ENABLED flag is on; and ia_sitemap.user_flows (4 populated flows on AltifyAI) is never read at all, despite the generator already receiving the full ia_sitemap object. All three are fixable read-side, inside this one file, using data the generator already has in hand (ia_sitemap.pages[].path resolves real routes without touching the flag). This must land before the chairman's clean-slate test venture reaches Stage 15 (ratification 212909b9) -- that venture is this fix's commissioning test. A 4th defect (positional screen_ref, screen-${idx}) is documented and explicitly deferred rather than folded in (TR-3), along with a pre-existing persona-matching gap unrelated to this SD's three defects (TR-5). REVISED after TESTING PLAN-phase review (evidence 85a34c05): the original PRD's FR-2 no-match example was factually wrong (measured against the live AltifyAI data below) and FR-2/FR-3's acceptance criteria were vacuously satisfiable against the actual measured data as first worded -- both are corrected below with exact, testable rules and fixture requirements.

functional_requirements.title: Story provenance: replace the synthesized-key fallback with a content-derived pointer, at all THREE call sites
functional_requirements.description: stage-15-user-journey.js has THREE places that fall back to a non-identifying value when story.id is absent (which it always is on live data -- lib/eva/blueprint-agents/user-story-pack.js's systemPrompt never asks for one): :188 (`story_refs: [entry.story.id || provisionalId]`), :340 (`generated_from.stories: cluster.stories.map(s => s.id||s.title||s.name).filter(Boolean)`), and :153 (`orphanStoryIds.push(story.id || story.title || story.name || slugify(...))`) -- the third site was missed in earlier scoping and must be included or the artifact ends up with TWO different identifier schemes for the same underlying stories (story_refs as content pointers, orphan_story_ids as slugified goal text). Add a pure function `computeStoryRef(story)` that returns `story.id` when present, else a content-derived pointer: `sty-<8hex>` where the hex is sha256 over a stable, order-independent serialization of ONLY {as_a, i_want_to, so_that} (deliberately excluding acceptance_criteria and other mutable/derived fields, so editing acceptance criteria -- a common, expected workflow action -- does not silently break story_refs continuity across regenerations). Use computeStoryRef(story) at all three sites, replacing every remaining reference to provisionalId, s.title, or s.name as a provenance fallback. NOTE (corrected per TESTING T-8): this is a DELIBERATE local design tradeoff for continuity, matching this file's own step_id carry-forward rule -- it is NOT mandated by ratification df3186e6, which is about a pointer carrying a *version or hash of the whole overwritable record*; hashing a chosen field subset means the pointer does NOT change when an excluded field (acceptance_criteria) changes, which is the opposite of version-fidelity. State plainly in code comments that story_refs does not detect acceptance_criteria drift -- this is accepted, not hidden.
acceptance_criteria: computeStoryRef(story) returns story.id verbatim when present (backward-compatible with any future producer that does emit one).

computeStoryRef(story) returns a sha256-derived 'sty-<8hex>' pointer when story.id is absent, computed ONLY over {as_a, i_want_to, so_that} (never acceptance_criteria or other mutable/derived fields).
Calling computeStoryRef on the SAME story content twice returns the IDENTICAL pointer (determinism) -- proven by a unit test.

ALL THREE sites use computeStoryRef: story_refs (:188), generated_from.stories (:340), and orphanStoryIds (:153) -- no remaining reference to provisionalId, s.title, or s.name as a provenance fallback ANYWHERE in the file.

Run against the FR-4 fixture (real measured AltifyAI shape, 0 stories with id): every generated step's story_refs[0] is a 'sty-' pointer, never a pipe-delimited composite string matching the step's own goal|screen_ref|action key; every orphan_story_id is ALSO a 'sty-' pointer, not a slugified goal-text string.

functional_requirements.title: Route resolution: read ia_sitemap.pages[].path instead of the flag-gated page_type
functional_requirements.description: stage-15-user-journey.js:183 (`route: entry.screen.page_type ? '/'+slugify(page_type) : null`) derives route from screen.page_type, which is only populated by stage-15-wireframe-generator.js when the absent, undocumented EVA_SURFACE_AWARE_ENABLED env flag is on -- making route null BY CONSTRUCTION on every live venture today, not intermittently. The generator already receives the full ia_sitemap object (ctx.wireframeScreensPayload.ia_sitemap, passed at stage-15.js:224) whose pages[] entries carry a real, always-populated `path` field (confirmed at stage-15-ia-generator.js normalizeIAResult:175-189). Resolve route by matching the mapped screen to an ia_sitemap page using the SAME case-insensitive name-equality match already used for the persona_relevance boost at line 111 (`p.name.toLowerCase() === screen.screen_name.toLowerCase()`), then use that page's `path`. When no IA page matches the screen name, route stays null AND the generator pushes an explicit ROUTE_UNRESOLVED finding onto the SAME top-level `findings` array generateUserJourneys already builds (matching PERSONA_PROVENANCE_MISSING/PERSONA_JOURNEY_MISSING/STEP_COVERAGE_MISSING's shape and placement -- there is no separate 'journey-level' findings array; buildStepsForGoalCluster must return a third field, e.g. `routeFindings`, alongside {steps, orphanStoryIds} so generateUserJourneys can push them onto its own findings array) -- NEVER fabricate a route, per this file's own doctrine (lines 8-9, 94-95, 142-143: 'absence is surfaced as a finding, never fabricated'). Do NOT read or depend on screen.page_type or EVA_SURFACE_AWARE_ENABLED at all -- that flag has cross-stage blast radius (Stage 18 marketing-copy) this SD does not need to touch. CORRECTED EXAMPLE (TESTING T-1 -- the original PRD named the wrong screens): on measured AltifyAI data, 'Integrations' and 'Subscription & Billing' BOTH have exact-matching IA pages ('Integrations'->/integrations, 'Subscription & Billing'->/settings/billing) and resolve fine. The ONLY screen with no exact IA page match is 'Signup/Registration' (the IA page is named 'Sign Up', a different string) -- but per TESTING T-2, that screen is never reached by any live step (0 stories map to it, so it never appears in a journey), meaning the ROUTE_UNRESOLVED path CANNOT be exercised by the raw measured data alone and the FR-4 fixture must be deliberately constructed to include a case where a REACHED screen has no matching page (see FR-4).
acceptance_criteria: route is resolved from ia_sitemap.pages[].path via case-insensitive screen-name-to-page-name matching -- zero remaining reads of screen.page_type or process.env.EVA_SURFACE_AWARE_ENABLED anywhere in this file.
When a screen's name matches an ia_sitemap page (case-insensitive), the step's route equals that page's path exactly.

When a screen's name matches NO ia_sitemap page, route is null AND a ROUTE_UNRESOLVED finding is pushed onto generateUserJourneys' top-level `findings` array (the SAME array PERSONA_PROVENANCE_MISSING etc. use), carrying at minimum {type:'ROUTE_UNRESOLVED', persona, journey_id, screen_ref, screen_name}. buildStepsForGoalCluster's return shape gains a third field carrying candidate route findings up to the caller.

Run against the FR-4 fixture, which is DELIBERATELY crafted (not a verbatim mirror of live data) to include at least one step whose screen IS reached by a story/step AND has no matching ia_sitemap page: that step has route:null AND produces a ROUTE_UNRESOLVED finding. Every OTHER step (whose screen does match a page) has a non-null route equal to that page's path.

The success criterion is honestly satisfiable: 'zero null routes among resolvable (reached) steps, and an explicit ROUTE_UNRESOLVED finding for every unresolvable one' -- NOT a literal 'zero null routes'. On the raw measured AltifyAI data specifically, all 14 live steps are expected to resolve to real, non-null routes post-fix (their screens all have exact IA page matches) and zero ROUTE_UNRESOLVED findings are expected there -- the unresolvable case is exercised only via the crafted portion of the FR-4 fixture, not the raw snapshot.

functional_requirements.title: Consume ia_sitemap.user_flows: exact ordered-subsequence coverage check over screen-resolvable flow steps, never silently ignored
functional_requirements.description: ia_sitemap.user_flows (stage-15-ia-generator.js normalizeIAResult:200-206, each entry {name, persona, steps: string[] (ordered PAGE names), description}) is never read anywhere in stage-15-user-journey.js today -- confirmed by a full-file grep returning zero hits, independently by two sub-agents. Read ctx.wireframeScreensPayload.ia_sitemap.user_flows alongside the existing .pages read (line 299). PERSONA MATCH (corrected per TESTING T-3 -- exact/case-insensitive equality does NOT work: measured journey persona_ref is 'The Busy Content Creator' while the matching flow's persona field is 'Busy Content Creator', no leading 'The'): use the SAME bidirectional case-insensitive substring match already implemented in clusterStoriesByGoal:62 (`asA.includes(personaLower) || personaLower.includes(asA)`), applied between journey.persona_ref and flow.persona. PERSONA-JOURNEY SEQUENCE, DEFINED (resolves TESTING R-1 -- a persona routinely has MULTIPLE journeys, one per goal-cluster/epic; measured 4 journeys per persona on live AltifyAI data, so 'that persona's journey step sequence' is otherwise undefined): the comparison sequence for a persona is the CONCATENATION of every journey whose persona_ref matches (via the same bidirectional substring rule), taken in their EMISSION order -- the order generateUserJourneys's own persona/cluster loop pushes them onto the `journeys` array (never re-sorted by any other key) -- with each journey's own steps in their existing internal order. COVERAGE RULE (corrected per TESTING T-4 -- the original 'substantially represented, in order' wording is untestable, and the original AC-3's strict 'ALL reachable in sequence' is dead-by-construction on real data since several AltifyAI flow steps name IA pages with NO corresponding wireframe screen at all, e.g. 'Login', 'Generation History', 'Team Management'): for each persona-matching flow, filter flow.steps to `resolvableSteps` -- those page names that match an ACTUAL screen in the venture (same case-insensitive name match as FR-2's route resolution). For every flow.step that does NOT resolve to any screen at all (not merely 'not reached', but no screen object exists with that name), push a FLOW_STEP_UNRESOLVED finding {type:'FLOW_STEP_UNRESOLVED', flow_name, page_name} -- this is informational and does not by itself fail the flow's coverage (per TESTING R-4: on measured AltifyAI data, flows 2 and 3 each have exactly ONE unresolvable step ['Login'] plus 5 resolvable ones, and are uncovered NOT because of that unresolvable step but because their 5 resolvable screens are never ALL reached, in order, within their persona's concatenated journey sequence -- the unresolvable-step case and the wrong-order/missing-screen case are genuinely different failure modes, both real in the measured data). Then check whether `resolvableSteps`, IN ORDER, form an exact (not fuzzy) ordered subsequence of that persona's CONCATENATED journey step sequence as defined above (matched by each step's resolved screen -- reuse FR-2's per-step route/screen resolution, not raw screen_ref). COVERED if yes; FLOW_COVERAGE_MISSING (pushed onto the same top-level findings array, {type:'FLOW_COVERAGE_MISSING', persona, flow_name}) if no. Add flows_total/flows_covered/uncovered_flows fields to computeCoverageSelfcheck's return shape (its exported signature changes to accept a 4th parameter carrying the flows + resolution inputs it needs -- state this explicitly as an intentional signature change, not an implicit one; computeCoverageSelfcheck and buildStepsForGoalCluster have zero callers outside this file and its own test file, so both signature changes are fully contained) -- the existing zero-personas early return (line ~307, which already has ia_sitemap in scope since screens/iaPages are computed at lines 298-299 BEFORE the personas.length check) must ALSO call computeCoverageSelfcheck with the flows data as its new 4th argument, populating flows_total as the venture's actual flow count, flows_covered:0, and uncovered_flows: all flow names -- never silently omitted or left at an implicit 0/undefined. Never fabricate journey steps to force flow coverage.
acceptance_criteria: ia_sitemap.user_flows is read from ctx.wireframeScreensPayload.ia_sitemap.user_flows -- confirmed by a grep showing at least one read of user_flows/userFlows in the file.

Persona matching between a journey and a flow uses the bidirectional case-insensitive substring rule from clusterStoriesByGoal:62 -- NOT exact/case-insensitive equality. A unit test proves 'The Busy Content Creator' (journey) matches 'Busy Content Creator' (flow) under this rule.

A persona's comparison sequence is the CONCATENATION of all persona-matching journeys in their emission (array push) order, each journey's own steps in their existing order -- a unit test proves this against a fixture persona with 2+ journeys (matching the real 4-journeys-per-persona shape), not a single-journey persona where the definition would be moot.

computeCoverageSelfcheck's signature and return object are both updated: it accepts the flows + per-step resolved-screen data it needs as an explicit 4th parameter, and returns flows_total, flows_covered, and uncovered_flows (array of flow names) in addition to its existing fields. The zero-personas early-return call site is updated to pass this same 4th argument (never calls computeCoverageSelfcheck with fewer arguments than the new signature requires).

Coverage is computed as an EXACT ordered-subsequence match of a flow's resolvableSteps (flow.steps filtered to those matching an actual screen) against the persona's CONCATENATED journey sequence (as defined above) -- not a fuzzy/'substantial' match, and not a single arbitrarily-chosen journey when the persona has more than one. A flow.step naming a page with NO corresponding screen at all produces a FLOW_STEP_UNRESOLVED finding and is excluded from the subsequence check (it does not automatically fail the flow) -- this is a DIFFERENT failure mode from a flow being uncovered because its resolvable steps are missing or out of order (FLOW_COVERAGE_MISSING); a test proves both findings can occur independently.
Run against the FR-4 fixture (see FR-4 AC-5/AC-6 for the exact covered/uncovered-with-wrong-order/uncovered-with-missing-screen requirements this exercises).

functional_requirements.title: Checked-in test fixture mirroring MEASURED producer output, deliberately crafted to exercise BOTH the resolvable and unresolvable branches of FR-2 and FR-3
functional_requirements.description: tests/unit/stage-15-user-journey.test.js's existing fixtures mask all three defects: every story literal hand-supplies id (never emitted by the real producer), every generateUserJourneys call passes ia_sitemap:{pages:[]} with no user_flows key at all, and the file contains zero assertions on route or user_flows -- which is exactly how 14/14 null routes and composite-string story_refs shipped green under SD-LEO-INFRA-FIRST-CLASS-USER-001 (23/23 existing tests pass green against the CURRENT, unfixed file -- that green result is itself the confirming evidence of the gap). Both live ventures with a blueprint_user_journey artifact (AltifyAI 50763b6a, ApexNiche 809ec7e7) are named for deletion under ratification 3c4a6781, so a live-venture-based test is not viable and the fixture must be checked in. Build a new fixture (a new tests/fixtures/stage-15-user-journey/ file, or inline in the test file -- implementer's choice) DERIVED FROM but not a byte-identical copy of the MEASURED AltifyAI shapes captured in scripts/one-off/fix-stage-journey-001-fixture-snapshot.json (captured live during this SD's LEAD phase, before any deletion): stories carrying {as_a, i_want_to, so_that, acceptance_criteria} (plus whatever other fields the real producer emits, e.g. story_points/mvp -- do NOT assert the story object has EXACTLY these fields and no others, only that id/title/name are absent) with NO id/title/name field; screens carrying page_type:null; ia_sitemap.pages with real populated path values. The fixture MUST be deliberately adjusted from the raw snapshot in the following ways the raw data cannot provide on its own (per TESTING T-2/T-4/R-1/R-2): (a) at least one screen that IS mapped to by a story (i.e., reached by a step) has no matching ia_sitemap page -- the raw data's one no-match screen ('Signup/Registration') is never reached, so either add a story that maps to it, or adjust the fixture's screen/page names so a reached screen loses its match; (b) give at least one persona 2+ journeys (the real, universal shape -- 4 journeys/persona on live data) so FR-3's concatenated-sequence rule is actually exercised, not vacuously true for a single-journey persona; (c) at least one user_flow that resolves as COVERED under FR-3's exact-subsequence rule, with >=3 resolvable steps appearing in the CORRECT order within its persona's concatenated journey sequence (a 1-step 'covered' flow would be trivially satisfiable without ever checking order -- TESTING R-2); (d) at least one user_flow that is uncovered specifically because its resolvable steps are present but in the WRONG order (not merely missing a screen) -- proving the subsequence check enforces ORDER, not just multiset membership; (e) the raw measured shape's own genuinely-uncovered flows (2 of the 4 real flows each have exactly one FLOW_STEP_UNRESOLVED-triggering page ['Login'] plus 5 resolvable-but-never-all-reached-in-order screens) remain represented so the FLOW_STEP_UNRESOLVED-without-auto-fail behavior is exercised too, distinct from (d)'s pure-ordering failure; (f) (added per TESTING R-7, confirmed by simulation: a deliberately-wrong implementation that auto-fails any flow containing an unresolvable step satisfies every OTHER fixture requirement above, since (c)/(d)/(e) each fail under it for reasons unrelated to that discriminator) at least one user_flow that HAS an unresolvable step (a page name with no corresponding screen at all) AND whose resolvable steps DO form a correct ordered subsequence of the persona's concatenated journey sequence -- expected result: COVERED, with a FLOW_STEP_UNRESOLVED finding present and NO FLOW_COVERAGE_MISSING finding for that flow. This is the only flow shape under which a correct implementation and an auto-fail-on-unresolvable-step implementation give different answers, so it is the load-bearing fixture case, not a nice-to-have.
acceptance_criteria: The new fixture's story objects carry no id, title, or name field -- matching the measured producer shape (other real fields like story_points/mvp/acceptance_criteria may be present, matching the actual producer output).
The new fixture's screen objects carry page_type:null.

The new fixture's ia_sitemap includes BOTH a non-empty pages[] (with real path values) and a non-empty user_flows[] -- the prior always-empty ia_sitemap:{pages:[]} pattern is not reused for the new FR-1/FR-2/FR-3 test cases (existing tests for OTHER concerns, e.g. clusterStoriesByGoal unit tests, may keep their existing minimal fixtures unchanged).

At least one fixture screen that IS reached by a generated step has NO matching ia_sitemap page (deliberately constructed, per the description) -- exercising FR-2's ROUTE_UNRESOLVED path, not just the raw data's always-unreached no-match screen.
At least one fixture persona has 2+ journeys, and a unit test asserts FR-3's coverage check against that persona uses the CONCATENATION of all of them in emission order (TESTING R-1).

At least one fixture user_flow is COVERED with >=3 resolvable steps in correct order (TESTING R-2 -- not a trivial 1-step flow); at least one fixture user_flow is UNCOVERED specifically due to WRONG ORDER of otherwise-present resolvable steps (TESTING R-2, proving the subsequence check enforces order); at least one fixture user_flow is UNCOVERED because its resolvable steps are never ALL reached in order by the persona's concatenated journey sequence, and SEPARATELY contains a step with no corresponding screen at all that raises a FLOW_STEP_UNRESOLVED finding WITHOUT itself causing the uncoverage (TESTING R-7b -- the unresolvable step is not the cause of coverage failure; the missing-in-order resolvable steps are, mirroring measured flows 2/3 exactly).

REQUIRED (TESTING R-7, the discriminating case): at least one fixture user_flow HAS an unresolvable step AND its resolvable steps DO form a correct ordered subsequence -- expected COVERED, with a FLOW_STEP_UNRESOLVED finding present and explicitly NO FLOW_COVERAGE_MISSING finding for that flow. A test must assert both the finding's presence AND the absence of FLOW_COVERAGE_MISSING for this specific flow, proving an unresolvable step alone never causes coverage failure.

New test assertions exist for: route is non-null and correct for resolvable/reached steps (FR-2); route is null WITH a ROUTE_UNRESOLVED finding for the deliberately-unresolvable reached step (FR-2); story_refs and orphan_story_ids are all 'sty-' content pointers, never composite pipe strings or slugified text (FR-1); flows_total/flows_covered/uncovered_flows are correct against the fixture's known covered/wrong-order-uncovered/missing-in-order-uncovered/covered-with-unresolvable-step flow answers, and FLOW_STEP_UNRESOLVED findings fire independently of FLOW_COVERAGE_MISSING findings in both directions (present without the other, per flow) (FR-3); calling generateUserJourneys twice on the identical fixture input produces IDENTICAL story_refs and routes (determinism, FR-1+FR-2).

technical_requirements.description: All changes are confined to lib/eva/stage-templates/analysis-steps/stage-15-user-journey.js and its test file/fixture -- lib/eva/stage-templates/stage-15-screens.js (the shared normalizer) and the EVA_SURFACE_AWARE_ENABLED flag are explicitly OUT OF SCOPE (VAL-5), since the generator already receives everything it needs (ia_sitemap.pages[].path, ia_sitemap.user_flows) without touching either.

No schema/migration changes (TESTING-confirmed: blueprint_user_journey's storage already exists via the pre-existing 20260710/20260711 migrations; the artifact content column is JSONB, so all new fields are additive; git status on database/migrations is clean for this SD). blueprint_user_journey's artifact shape gains no new top-level fields except coverage_selfcheck.flows_total/flows_covered/uncovered_flows (additive) and findings entries of new types ROUTE_UNRESOLVED/FLOW_COVERAGE_MISSING/FLOW_STEP_UNRESOLVED (additive to an existing array) -- no breaking change to any existing consumer's read shape. Unit tests via vitest are the correct and sufficient test tier -- every function under change is pure and exported; no ephemeral-DB DDL tier is needed for this SD.

DEFERRED, NOT IN SCOPE: the positional screen_ref (screen-${idx}) defect. A durable fix requires either widening the shared stage-15-screens.js normalizer (re-opening SD-LEO-INFRA-S15-WIREFRAME-SCREENS-REGRESSION-001's territory) or a second, local content-stable screen-identity scheme whose interaction with computeCoverageSelfcheck's screen-reachability accounting (which currently keys on the SAME screen_id/screen_ref for both 'which screens exist' and 'which were reached') needs its own design pass to avoid silently changing what counts as an unreachable screen. Recorded here as a named, deliberate deferral (not a silent omission) per VALIDATION/Explore's own recommendation; a follow-up SD may pick it up once this fix lands and the fixture infrastructure from FR-4 exists to test against.

The captured live fixture data lives at scripts/one-off/fix-stage-journey-001-fixture-snapshot.json (raw, untrimmed, unmodified). FR-4's checked-in test fixture is a DERIVED, deliberately-adjusted subset of it (per FR-4's two required constructions), not a verbatim copy -- the raw snapshot may be deleted from the worktree once FR-4's fixture is committed, or kept as a one-off reference; it must never be treated as the test fixture verbatim (besides needing the two deliberate adjustments, it also includes full unrelated fields like personas/epics/financial data not needed for these tests).

DEFERRED, PRE-EXISTING, NOT INTRODUCED BY THIS SD: 4 of the 18 measured AltifyAI stories carry generic as_a values ('new user', 'returning user', 'user' x2) that match NO persona under clusterStoriesByGoal:62's bidirectional-substring rule, so the entire epic those stories belong to contributes zero stories to any journey, silently, with no finding raised. This is why the live artifact's coverage_selfcheck reports stories_total:14, not 18 -- a reviewer comparing FR-4's fixture (built from the same 18-story measured shape) against the live artifact's 14 should not mistake that gap for a regression this SD introduced. Fixing the generic-as_a matching gap is out of scope here; noted as a candidate for a future SD.

test_scenarios.scenario: generateUserJourneys runs against the FR-4 fixture's UNMODIFIED-from-measured-shape portion (stories with no id, screens with page_type:null, the screens/pages that DO exactly match by name)
test_scenarios.expected: Every step's story_refs[0] and every orphan_story_id is a deterministic 'sty-<8hex>' content pointer; steps whose screen matches an ia_sitemap page have route equal to that page's path exactly.

test_scenarios.scenario: generateUserJourneys runs against the FR-4 fixture's DELIBERATELY-CONSTRUCTED portion: a reached screen with no matching ia_sitemap page, and a flow with a resolvable page-step naming a screen that doesn't exist
test_scenarios.expected: The reached-but-unmatched screen's step has route:null plus a ROUTE_UNRESOLVED finding; the flow's unresolvable page-step produces a FLOW_STEP_UNRESOLVED finding and is excluded from that flow's coverage subsequence check (rather than automatically failing coverage for a reason unrelated to journey generation quality).

test_scenarios.scenario: generateUserJourneys is called twice in a row against the IDENTICAL fixture input
test_scenarios.expected: Both runs produce identical story_refs, orphan_story_ids, and route values for every step (determinism -- content-hash pointers and name-join route resolution are both pure functions of the input, not the invocation).

test_scenarios.scenario: A journey with persona_ref 'The Busy Content Creator' is checked for coverage against a user_flow whose persona field is 'Busy Content Creator' (no leading 'The')
test_scenarios.expected: The bidirectional substring match correctly pairs them -- coverage is evaluated for this flow against this journey, not skipped as a persona mismatch.

test_scenarios.scenario: The FR-4 fixture's deliberately-constructed fully-coverable flow, and its genuinely-uncoverable flow (mirroring the real AltifyAI shape)
test_scenarios.expected: flows_covered and uncovered_flows correctly distinguish the two -- flows_total equals the fixture's total flow count, and the split matches a manual trace of the fixture (asserted by a dedicated unit test, not eyeballed).

test_scenarios.scenario: A story with NO id, title, or name (the measured real-world shape) is processed by computeStoryRef twice with the same as_a/i_want_to/so_that content
test_scenarios.expected: Both calls return the identical 'sty-<8hex>' pointer; a story with DIFFERENT as_a/i_want_to/so_that content returns a DIFFERENT pointer; a story whose acceptance_criteria are edited but whose as_a/i_want_to/so_that are unchanged returns the SAME pointer as before the edit.

test_scenarios.scenario: generateUserJourneys is called with zero Stage-10 personas (the existing early-return path at line ~307)
test_scenarios.expected: coverage_selfcheck still populates flows_total/flows_covered/uncovered_flows correctly (flows_total = the venture's flow count, flows_covered = 0, uncovered_flows = all flow names) rather than silently omitting or defaulting these fields.

risks.risk: A literal 'zero null routes' success criterion, if implemented naively, would pressure the fix into fabricating routes for screens with no real IA page match -- directly violating this file's own stated never-fabricate doctrine and producing dishonest journey data.
risks.mitigation: FR-2 explicitly restates the criterion as 'zero null routes among resolvable (reached) steps + an explicit ROUTE_UNRESOLVED finding for every unresolvable one', matching the file's existing findings-array pattern rather than trading honesty for a green number.

risks.risk: TESTING PLAN-phase review found the raw measured AltifyAI data CANNOT exercise either FR-2's ROUTE_UNRESOLVED path or FR-3's covered-flow path (the one no-match screen is never reached; all 4 real flows include at least one screenless page-step) -- a fixture built as a verbatim copy of the snapshot would produce vacuous tests that pass against a stub implementation.
risks.mitigation: FR-4 explicitly requires the fixture to be DELIBERATELY constructed (not verbatim) to include both branches: a reached screen with no page match, and a fully-coverable flow -- both spelled out as acceptance criteria, not left to implementer judgment.

risks.risk: The only two ventures with a real blueprint_user_journey artifact (AltifyAI, ApexNiche) are both named for deletion under ratification 3c4a6781, which could happen at any time -- a live-venture-dependent test plan would become untestable with no warning.
risks.mitigation: The live fixture data was captured to scripts/one-off/fix-stage-journey-001-fixture-snapshot.json during this SD's LEAD phase (2026-09-14), independent of and before any deletion. FR-4's checked-in fixture is derived from that captured snapshot, not a live query.

risks.risk: Folding in the positional screen_ref fix (C4) without a proper design pass could silently change computeCoverageSelfcheck's screen-reachability semantics (it currently uses the same screen_id for both 'all screens' and 'reached screens'), producing a regression that looks like an improvement.
risks.mitigation: TR-3 explicitly defers C4 out of this SD's scope with a written rationale, rather than rushing a second identity scheme under this SD's time pressure.

consumers: lib/eva/bridge/orchestrator-journey-steps.js deriveJourneySteps() -- reads step.route directly and passes it through to downstream UAT-walking; this is the primary motivation for FR-2's route-resolution fix, and gains real routes for the first time.

lib/eva/stage-templates/analysis-steps/stage-15-coverage-disposition-reader.js -- reads coverage_selfcheck.unreachable_screens against venture_screen_dispositions; unaffected in shape by FR-1/FR-2/FR-3's additive fields, but should be spot-checked post-merge since it shares the coverage_selfcheck object.

Stage 16 (whatever reads blueprint_user_journey next in the pipeline) -- not independently confirmed to read story_refs or generated_from.stories in this PRD's research pass; FR-1's change is additive/backward-compatible regardless (any reader treating story_refs as an opaque string continues to work).
dependencies: ia_sitemap.pages[].path and ia_sitemap.user_flows[] -- both already produced by stage-15-ia-generator.js and already passed into the journey generator via ctx.wireframeScreensPayload.ia_sitemap; no upstream change needed.
scripts/one-off/fix-stage-journey-001-fixture-snapshot.json -- the captured live data FR-4's fixture derives from.
data_contracts: blueprint_user_journey's step shape gains no new fields (route and story_refs are populated more accurately, not restructured); the artifact's TOP-LEVEL coverage_selfcheck (a sibling of journeys, not a per-journey field -- generateUserJourneys returns {journeys, coverage_selfcheck, findings} at its top level, and no journey object itself carries a coverage_selfcheck or findings field) gains 3 new additive fields (flows_total, flows_covered, uncovered_flows), computed via computeCoverageSelfcheck's now-changed signature (accepts flows + resolution data as a new parameter); the artifact's TOP-LEVEL findings array gains 3 new finding types (ROUTE_UNRESOLVED, FLOW_COVERAGE_MISSING, FLOW_STEP_UNRESOLVED), same array shape as existing types. buildStepsForGoalCluster's return shape gains a third field (route findings) alongside its existing {steps, orphanStoryIds}.
runtime_config: No new env vars. EVA_SURFACE_AWARE_ENABLED is explicitly NOT read by this fix (TR-1).
observability_rollout: No feature flag needed -- this is a bug fix to an existing, already-live generator; the next Stage-15 run for any venture (starting with the clean-slate test venture per ratification 212909b9) picks up the fix automatically.

components.name: lib/eva/stage-templates/analysis-steps/stage-15-user-journey.js
components.role: The generator itself -- all 3 fixes (FR-1/FR-2/FR-3) land here, read-side only. computeCoverageSelfcheck's signature changes (FR-3); buildStepsForGoalCluster's return shape gains a third field (FR-2).

components.name: lib/eva/stage-templates/analysis-steps/stage-15-ia-generator.js
components.role: Unchanged -- already produces ia_sitemap.pages[].path and ia_sitemap.user_flows[]; this PRD only adds READERS of its existing output.

components.name: tests/unit/stage-15-user-journey.test.js (+ new fixture)
components.role: FR-4 -- gains a realistic, deliberately-adjusted fixture and new assertions covering all 3 fixes' resolvable AND unresolvable branches.

components.name: lib/eva/bridge/orchestrator-journey-steps.js
components.role: Unchanged consumer -- gains real, non-null routes for the first time as a side effect of FR-2.

implementation_approach.summary: FR-4's fixture-building work happens first (or in parallel), since FR-1/FR-2/FR-3 all need it to prove they are non-vacuous, not just that they don't crash on the old always-empty fixture -- and the fixture requires deliberate construction (not a verbatim snapshot copy) per FR-2/FR-3's blocking-branch requirements. Implementation order: FR-4 (fixture, including its two deliberate constructions), FR-1 (provenance, fully local and independent), FR-2 (routes, introduces the screen-name-to-ia-page match helper that FR-3 also needs, plus buildStepsForGoalCluster's third return field), FR-3 (flows, reuses FR-2's match helper, changes computeCoverageSelfcheck's signature). One PR expected given the contained diff (all changes in one production file + its test file/fixture); commits split per FR for reviewability.

smoke_test_steps.instruction: Run `npx vitest run tests/unit/stage-15-user-journey.test.js` after implementing FR-1..FR-4.
smoke_test_steps.expected_outcome: All existing tests plus the new FR-1/FR-2/FR-3 assertions pass; zero regressions in the pre-existing clusterStoriesByGoal/mapStoryToScreen/assignDurableStepIds/isValidDag test coverage.

smoke_test_steps.instruction: Manually invoke generateUserJourneys with the FR-4 fixture data in a scratch script and inspect one journey's steps.
smoke_test_steps.expected_outcome: story_refs and orphan_story_ids are 'sty-' pointers (not pipe-delimited composites or slugified text); the deliberately-constructed reached-unmatched screen has route:null and a ROUTE_UNRESOLVED finding; every other reached screen has a real route; coverage_selfcheck includes correct flows_total/flows_covered/uncovered_flows.

smoke_test_steps.instruction: Grep the modified file for 'page_type' and 'EVA_SURFACE_AWARE_ENABLED'.
